transcript.text: In the previous lectures, we discussed some problems based on translational mechanical systems. Now in this presentation, we are going to discuss a new concept which is Analogous Systems. So let's get started. In this lecture, we'll be discussing the analogy between mechanical systems and electrical systems. Yes, there exists a similarity between mechanical systems and electrical systems and their equilibrium equations. And that's why it is possible to draw an electrical system which will behave exactly similar to the given mechanical system. So we can say that for a given mechanical system, we can draw an electrical network which will behave exactly similar to this mechanical system. And this electrical system is called as the electrical analogous of the given mechanical system. There are two methods by which we can obtain the electrical analogous networks. The first method is the force-voltage analogy and the second method is the force-current analogy. In case of force-voltage analogy, the force in mechanical systems is assumed as analogous with the voltage of the electrical network. So if we assume the voltage of the electrical network to be analogous with the force of mechanical system and accordingly, if we derive the other analogous terms, we can draw the electrical analogous network. In the same way, in force-current analogy, the force in mechanical systems is assumed as analogous with the current of the electrical network. So if we assume the current of electrical network to be analogous with the force in mechanical systems and if we derive the other terms accordingly, then in that case, we can draw the electrical analogous network to the given mechanical system. For that sake, let us consider this mechanical system in which we are having a mass m which is connected with a spring from one side and the spring is connected to a fixed support from the other side. There is a friction between the fixed surface and this mass m which is indicated by the damper having the coefficient of viscous friction equal to b. We are applying a force f of t on this mass to the right hand side and due to this, there is a displacement x of t to the right hand side. Let us now define the equation of motion for this mechanical system. We have to analyze the number of forces acting on mass m. So what are the forces acting on mass m? Yes, the first force is the applied force f of t and due to this force, there is an opposing force in the spring which will act on the left hand side. There will be an opposing force in this damper which will try to oppose the relative motion and there will be a force of acceleration due to the mass m. So we can say that the first opposing force is force of acceleration which is equal to m multiplied with a where m is the mass of system and a is the acceleration caused in that system. The second opposing force is the force of friction which is b multiplied with v where b is the coefficient of viscous friction and v is the velocity of the system and the third opposing force is the restoring force of spring which is equal to k multiplied with x t where k is the spring constant and x t is the displacement in the spring.
